A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WaveVerse, with the same authors, core framework, and retained experiments. The text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite extensive reformatting and added evaluations.

before.justification: v1 reports original motion-generation benchmarks and ablations, RF phase-coherence simulations, and downstream imaging and activity-recognition experiments in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds baseline comparisons, real-measurement and HFSS validation, robustness analyses, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The state-aware transformer, path masking, motion tokenizer, A* planning, and spatial/temporal phase-coherent ray-tracing procedures remain substantively unchanged. The frequency-dependent material model and material-selection workflow already appear in v1 Figure 19. v2 adds material-curation and precomputation details without establishing a change to the underlying method.

E1.justification: v2 adds direct signal-fidelity evaluation using newly collected radar-camera measurements of walking and daily activities against glass, drywall, brick, and metal backgrounds, plus multiple frequency configurations. It also adds HFSS validation across four scenes and four radar poses per scene. These substantially expand test scenarios beyond the retained motion, respiration, imaging, and activity-recognition evaluations.

E2.justification: v2 adds MotionLCM to motion-generation and timing comparisons, Standard RT to imaging augmentation, RF Genesis to activity-recognition augmentation, and HFSS to signal-fidelity comparisons. Standard ray tracing already appeared in v1's phase-coherence tests, but its participation in the downstream augmentation comparison is new. These additions are supported by reported results, not merely citations.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce WHAM reconstruction of synchronized camera observations, range-time comparisons using PSNR and energy similarity, and a four-scene-by-four-radar-pose HFSS protocol with diffraction/refraction controls. v2 also adds skating, bone-length, collision, and generation-success measurements. The retained motion-training settings, downstream splits, and augmentation budgets do not show corresponding substantive revisions.

E4.justification: v2 adds a state-only removal ablation in Table 2 and pooling, independent-masking, and input-perturbation studies in Appendix Table 6. It also evaluates physical plausibility, scene-generation failures and collisions, frequency robustness, material misassignment, and the effect of enabling diffraction/refraction in HFSS. These substantially extend v1's component and masking-hyperparameter analyses.

E5.justification: Appendix A.2.2 newly specifies that component-runtime measurements are averaged over 10 runs. This is a limited addition of repeat-count information for a new analysis, not evidence that retained benchmarks received more runs. Neither version reports confidence intervals or formal significance tests for the main performance comparisons.

E6.justification: Existing motion-benchmark and downstream augmentation scores are retained, but v2 adds substantial results. Examples include 71.6% versus RF Genesis's 54.6% accuracy at 19× augmentation, 28.63 dB PSNR against collected signals, and HFSS agreement of 33.57 dB without diffraction/refraction versus 31.25 dB with them. New ablation, robustness, physical-plausibility, and runtime results further expand the evidence.

T1.justification: The motion-token probability model, channel impulse response, vertex-group path expansion, and frequency-dependent dielectric formulas remain mathematically equivalent. Indexing and notation are clarified, but no substantive theoretical derivation, assumption, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The central contributions of scalable path-conditioned world generation and phase-coherent RF simulation remain. v2 removes the explicit first-time RF-imaging data-generation claim and adds a comparative claim that augmentation scales better than competing RF simulation methods. The new real-measurement/HFSS evidence primarily strengthens the existing signal-realism claim.

C2.justification: v2 adds a token-imbalance explanation for path overfitting and explicitly attributes gains to the proposed components rather than autoregression itself. It interprets sensitivity to material mismatch and the limited diffraction/refraction effects in tested setups, explains scene-generation failures, and expands applicability limitations and future directions to fine-grained interactions and real-data refinement.

D1.justification: v2 adds MotionLCM adaptation details, material-curation information, pipeline timing and hardware, ray counts, antenna configuration, CUDA acceleration, and real-measurement reconstruction details. Code and simulator availability changes from a promised release to a reported release. Conversely, v1's explicit Sionna/Mitsuba implementation and licensing paragraph, 60 cm clearance setting, and failed-path retry description disappear.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially revises positioning around phase coherence and the constraints imposed by time-indexed trajectories. It incorporates CASTER, Chen et al.'s 2025 RF modeling work, MotionLCM, and newer scene-interaction methods. v1's emphasis on short-duration scene-motion datasets is replaced by discussion of missing text control and required temporal inputs. This exceeds bibliographic updating.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and substantial explanatory passages are rewritten. Scene evaluation is folded into Section 4.1, the discussion becomes a standalone conclusion, limitations move to the appendix, and societal impacts move into the main document. The appendix gains a more detailed subsection hierarchy, substantially changing the narrative organization.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from a single-column layout to a two-column conference format. Figure 1 explicitly adds prompt and sensor-configuration inputs; retained figures are resized or rearranged. New baseline and ablation tables, a panoramic-imaging gallery, and real/HFSS comparison panels materially expand the displays. The Doppler figure expands to four timestamps.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important gaps in v1's validation through direct real-measurement/HFSS comparisons, material and frequency robustness checks, and competing-simulator augmentation results in Tables 3–4 and Appendix A.3.3. The isolated state ablation and alternative regularization studies also strengthen component attribution. These gains substantially improve support for fidelity, usefulness, and design choices, outweighing the loss of some implementation disclosures.
